title: On Degeneracies of Density, Magnetic, and Pairing Responses: How Competing Orders Echo Underlying Symmetries in the Hubbard Model
authors: Michael Meixner, Herbert Eßl, Matthias Reitner, Alessandro Toschi, Thomas Schäfer
abstract: Strongly correlated electron systems often display competing or even intertwined ordering tendencies, hinting to extremely close or degenerate many-electron energies. While degeneracies are directly rooted in the underlying symmetries of the problem under investigation, their multifaceted effects on different response functions and their mutual relations often remain elusive. Here we put this subject on a rigorous basis by investigating the degeneracies of charge, spin, and pairing susceptibilities for the unfrustrated, bipartite Hubbard model. Exploiting its pseudospin symmetry, we analytically derive the mutual relations between these response functions for generic spatial modulations, highly relevant, e.g., for the competition of stripe and superconducting orders. By means of two-particle numerical simulations we demonstrate the occurrence of a simultaneous $d$-wave pairing/$d$-density wave (loop current) instability in the vicinity of the metal-insulator transition, driven by short-ranged spin fluctuations for the two-dimensional case. We show how this degeneracy is gradually lifted by geometrical frustration, which favors superconductivity. Our study provides a general tool for revealing symmetry relations in correlated electron systems and establishes a unifying perspective on the nature of their intermingled charge/loop current, pairing, and spin orders.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes how charge, spin, and pairing instabilities are related by symmetry in the Hubbard model. It shows that these responses exhibit degeneracies due to pseudospin symmetry, confirming simultaneous CDW/SC instabilities numerically. The framework provides a powerful tool for understanding competing orders in strongly correlated materials.
main_problem: The study investigates degeneracies between charge, spin, and pairing susceptibilities that arise from underlying symmetries in strongly correlated electron systems.
main_result: The analysis analytically derives mutual relations showing that these three response functions are degenerate for the unfrustrated Hubbard model, a degeneracy lifted by geometrical frustration or symmetry breaking ($t'$).
method: The work combines analytical derivations exploiting pseudospin symmetries (SU(2)P) with advanced numerical techniques like Cluster Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (CDMFT) and Bethe-Salpeter Equation (BSE) analysis.
model_or_system: The primary model is the Hubbard Hamiltonian, studied on a bipartite lattice. The analysis focuses on how competing orders—charge density waves (CDW), spin density waves (SDW), and superconductivity (SC)—interact through their respective susceptibilities.
key_observables: Charge susceptibility ($\chi^{ch}$), spin susceptibility ($\chi^{sp}$), and pairing/superconducting susceptibility ($\chi^{pp}$) for various form factors (s, d, sext).
important_parameters: The Hubbard interaction strength ($U$), hopping parameters ($t, t'$), doping levels, and momentum transfer vectors ($q_{ph}$).
main_assumptions: Initial analytical results are rigorously derived for the unfrustrated, bipartite Hubbard model; numerical extensions rely on approximations like CDMFT.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate symmetry relations between response functions (Fig. 1), show concomitant divergences of d-wave CDW and SC susceptibilities at $T_c$ in CDMFT (Fig. 2a), and map out how introducing $t'$ gradually lifts these degeneracies (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing exact symmetry relations using pseudospin symmetry, to demonstrating the degeneracy numerically via CDMFT simulations, and finally analyzing how breaking symmetries ($t'$) or moving beyond simple lattice limits affects this fundamental relationship.
why_interesting: While focused on Hubbard model physics, the rigorous mathematical framework linking multiple response functions through underlying symmetries provides a general tool for understanding correlated quantum matter, which is relevant to many-body dynamics in AMO systems.
